description: Sahuaro Space es un equipo apasionado enfocado en conectar el desarrollo de software, la gestión de datos y el hardware con la ciencia planetaria y la exploración espacial.
summary: ELOISE is a mission care system that gives every astronaut a companion that listens and a system that watches over their body during long missions to the Moon and Mars. Each crew member chooses a character (Luma, Pipo or Nix) to talk to by text or live voice; the companion listens without judging, remembers what matters to them and, when the conversation suggests low mood or anxiety, offers validated screening questionnaires (PHQ-9, GAD-7). At the same time, ELOISE monitors radiation dose against the career limit, blood and cabin oxygen, CO2, heart rate, sleep and mood, raises alerts by urgency, opens a shelter mode during solar storms and keeps the flight surgeon informed through a live dashboard. It addresses two of NASA's biggest human-spaceflight hazards, radiation and isolation, which meet in the storm shelter. Conversations never leave the astronaut's phone: privacy is what makes a companion trustworthy instead of a watchdog.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
ELOISE gives every astronaut a companion that listens and a system that watches over their body.
- Companion that listens: each astronaut chooses Luma (empathetic), Pipo (funny) or Nix (analytical), each with its own voice, personality and 24 animated poses. The default mode only listens; companion mode talks back and suggests countermeasures NASA already uses (rest, a window, plants, a message home).
- Live voice mode: a near-real-time spoken conversation. The character listens, thinks, answers with its own voice and expressions chosen by the AI, then listens again on its own. The astronaut can interrupt at any time.
- Long-term memory: the companion remembers durable facts (for example, "listening to jazz helps before sleeping"), shared by the three characters, encrypted on the phone, visible and deletable by the astronaut.
- Validated screening: when the conversation suggests low mood or anxiety, the character offers (never forces) PHQ-2/PHQ-9 or GAD-2/GAD-7 with one-tap buttons. Questions are shown word for word and scoring uses the published cut-offs in code, never the AI. A positive answer on PHQ-9 item 9 starts the safety protocol.
- Safety protocol: self-harm or acute-panic signals trigger an offer to alert the flight surgeon; only the type and time are sent, and only after the astronaut confirms.
- Health and radiation monitoring: radiation dose (daily, mission and career against the 600 mSv limit), SpO2, cabin O2, CO2 and pressure, heart and breathing rate, sleep, and a one-minute daily check-in of mood, stress, energy and symptoms.
- Alerts and shelter mode: three alert levels with escalation, de-duplication and auto-resolution. A solar storm of S3 or higher opens a shelter session in the most shielded zone and assigns the crew.
- Flight surgeon dashboard: the whole crew in real time, alerts, radiation and space weather, a daily report for Earth, and a demo console that simulates sensors, solar storms and failures.

HOW IT WORKS
Android app (Kotlin + Compose Multiplatform) connected to Supabase (Postgres with row-level security and triggers for alerts, dose and shelter) and to a web dashboard. A Node.js server keeps all secret keys and runs the AI companion (OpenAI model with a strict JSON output: reply, risk, emotion, new memories and suggested questionnaire), the character voices (ElevenLabs) and the sensor simulator. On-device speech recognition is used when available, and without the AI the app answers in a basic local mode. A spacecraft version would run speech and language models on board, without internet.

PRIVACY BY DESIGN
Physical safety data is always shared with the surgeon; mood and sleep trends only with permission, revocable at any time; conversations, memory and questionnaire answers never leave the phone.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT
Lower radiation exposure through timely shelter alerts and dose tracking; earlier detection of mood, anxiety and sleep problems; a companion available when Earth is minutes away; and trust, because the astronaut controls what is shared. Next we want to test ELOISE in an analog mission (HERA or CHAPEA), move the AI and voice models on board, add per-zone dose maps, and have clinicians validate the screening protocol and thresholds.

CREATIVITY
Three characters with distinct personalities, voices and animated emotions turn health monitoring into a relationship instead of a form, while the screening and safety logic stays deterministic and testable.

TOOLS
Kotlin, Compose Multiplatform, Ktor, kotlinx.serialization, Android SpeechRecognizer and Keystore (AES-GCM); Node.js; HTML/CSS/JavaScript dashboard; Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Realtime, RLS); OpenAI API; ElevenLabs text-to-speech; PGlite and node:test; Gradle. Spec-driven development: 11 specifications, an OpenAPI contract and 60 automated tests. All sensor data in the demo is simulated.
